title: Some posts are maps. Some are sketches.
text:
DATA SCIENCE  ENERGY NETWORKS  DECISION MODELLING


I am a data scientist working on the systems that keep the gas flowing — asset risk, network data and the decisions a regulated utility has to justify with evidence. This is where I think out loud about it.


Currently Lead Data Scientist, Wales & West Utilities


Studying MSc Data Science, University of St Andrews


Interested in Applied decision science for energy & infrastructure
Most data science writing is about models. Comparatively little is about the messy, regulated, consequential systems models get deployed into — where a wrong number becomes a wrong investment, and a regulator will ask you to show your working. That is the part I find interesting, and it is what I write about.

title: Work
text: I work where data science meets regulated infrastructure: gas distribution, asset risk and the evidence a regulator expects behind an investment case. Below is the shape of that work — not a CV, which is what LinkedIn is for.

title: Work
section: Risk on a real asset base
text:
Risk on a real asset base
Network risk models are only as good as the asset data underneath them, and that data is rarely as complete as the model assumes. A lot of my work is the unglamorous part: establishing what is actually known about an asset population, what is inferred, and what is simply asserted — then being honest about which is which.

The interesting question is rarely “what does the model say”. It is “what would have to be true for the model to be wrong”.

title: Work
section: AI with a regulator in the room
text:
AI with a regulator in the room
Setting a direction for AI inside a utility is a different problem from setting one inside a tech company. The constraint is not capability — it is assurance, evidence, and the ability to explain a decision years after it was made. I am interested in the versions of this that survive scrutiny.

title: Work
text:
Decision modelling
Optimisation and scenario work aimed at an actual decision: what to do, in what order, under what budget. Scheduling, siting, prioritisation — problems where the answer has to be defensible as well as optimal.

title: Work
text:
Tools
R and Python for the modelling, Quarto for everything that has to be read by someone else, and a long-standing conviction that a well-made document is part of the work rather than an afterthought.
